narration: Okay, so picture a freelance graphic designer. They wake up at 7 a.m. They haven't even thrown the covers off yet. Still in bed. Still in bed.
explainedBy: Passage idea: clearing the deck first is a mirage - the easy emails eat the day and the most important task never starts. This beat sets the start: the designer lies in bed at 7 a.m., the day not begun.

storyboard.claim: A freelance designer wakes at 7 a.m., still in bed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The everyman lying in bed in her home workstation room, a clock beside her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: New stage: from the office MIT setup to one designer's morning at home, lying in bed at 7 a.m.
storyboard.addedInformation: The time and the situation: the day has not started yet.

narration: They reach over to the nightstand and grab their phone, which was charging face down. The screen lights up and there's a notification.
explainedBy: Passage idea: the easy tasks eat the day and the most important task never starts. This beat adds the trigger: before getting up, she picks up her phone and it lights up.

storyboard.claim: Still in bed, the designer grabs the phone and sees a notification.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer, same room; now she holds the phone and the phone icon replaces the clock.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person and room; the clock gives way to the phone, now in her hand.
storyboard.addedInformation: The phone enters the morning before anything else.

narration: 52 unread emails. Just an immediate punch in the gut. Immediately before they've even had water, their internal monologue starts negotiating.
explainedBy: Passage idea: the inbox pulls attention before the important task can start. This beat adds the hit: 52 unread emails, and she slumps, worried.

storyboard.claim: The 52 unread emails land as a punch in the gut and the mind starts negotiating.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer holding the same phone, now slumped with a worried face.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same phone in hand; her face turns worried and her body slumps; the count 52 appears.
storyboard.addedInformation: The size of the inbox and its emotional hit.

narration: Okay. I have that massive logo redesign due tomorrow, which requires deep creative thought.
explainedBy: Passage idea: the important task competes with the inbox. This beat adds the most important task: the big logo redesign due tomorrow, which needs deep thought.

storyboard.claim: The real priority is the logo redesign due tomorrow.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer, phone put down, thinking; a target (the most important task) appears beside her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person and room; the phone leaves her hand and the target - the big task - appears; slump becomes think.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the most important task and its deadline.

narration: But let me just knock out these quick emails Just clear the deck. Exactly. Let me pay that one server invoice.
explainedBy: Passage idea: the easy tasks pull her away from the important one. This beat adds the choice: the target stays there, but she picks the phone back up to knock out quick emails first.

storyboard.claim: She decides to clear quick emails and pay an invoice first.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer; the target is still on screen but she holds the phone again.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same target stays; she takes the phone back in hand and stops thinking about the task.
storyboard.addedInformation: The turn away from the priority toward small tasks.

narration: Let me reply to that quick client question. I'll just clear the deck, get to inbox zero, and then I'll have a totally clean slate to focus on the big logo project.
explainedBy: Passage idea: the easy tasks keep coming before the important one. This beat adds the plan: answer everything, reach inbox zero, then do the logo - the target still waits.

storyboard.claim: She plans to reach inbox zero first, then focus on the logo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer, still holding the phone, talking herself through the plan; the target still waits beside her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same phone and target; she now talks (the reasoning) and the label changes to inbox zero.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the promise of a clean slate later is carried by the label.

narration: And we both know exactly how that story Oh, completely. It's 2 p.m., the inbox is empty, and they haven't drawn a single vector line.
explainedBy: Passage idea: the easy tasks eat the day. This beat shows the result: it is 2 p.m., the inbox is done, and the logo has not been started - she slumps with the phone.
noVisual: The empty inbox and the undrawn logo cannot be drawn; the clock shows the lost hours and the label states the result.

storyboard.claim: By 2 p.m. the inbox is empty and no work on the logo has been done.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer with the phone, slumped and worried; the clock returns in place of the target.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person and phone; the target is replaced by the clock (the morning is gone) and she slumps, worried.
storyboard.addedInformation: The cost: the day is spent and the important task never began.

narration: The clearing the deck instinct is a psychological mirage. Theres McCann, a brilliant professor at the University of Missouri St. Louis, spent years researching this exact phenomenon.
explainedBy: Passage idea: clearing the deck first is a mirage. This beat names it: the instinct she just followed is rejected - struck out - while she looks at the phone that ate her day.
noVisual: A 'mirage' and the researcher (Theresa McCann) are not in the vocabulary; the struck label carries the rejection.

storyboard.claim: The clearing-the-deck instinct is a psychological mirage, studied by a researcher.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer holding the phone, sad and thinking; the instinct's name is struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person and phone; the clock leaves, the face turns sad and reflective, and the instinct is struck out.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the habit as an illusion.

narration: What did she find? She proved that the foundation of high performance and low stress isn't how fast you answer emails.
explainedBy: Passage idea: answering the inbox first is not what drives performance. This beat adds the finding: speed of email replies is struck out, and the target - the important task - comes back.

storyboard.claim: High performance does not come from answering emails fast.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Same designer with the phone; the target returns beside her while 'how fast you answer emails' is struck out.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Same person and phone; the target returns and the struck label now rejects email speed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the answer (do the most important task first) in the next beat.
